issues.basis: NL8; transition group NL8; FCSTM transition:line:15; InMotion state:line:11; finite reachability facts refuting InMotion and Accelerating reachability.
issues.expected: When motion begins, the InMotion scope must operationally enter Accelerating.
issues.observed: The InMotion initial transition exists but InMotion and Accelerating are unreachable from the top-level initial entry; Entry_Accelerate has no reachable consumer.
issues.reason: The exact InMotion initial edge targets Accelerating and carries Entry_Accelerate, but InMotion itself is unreachable from the root initial state. Therefore the required motion-begins entry is not operationally reachable in the closed finite graph.
issues.requirement_quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The local initial edge and its event consumer are declared exactly, so this issue concerns operational reachability rather than missing declaration or endpoint.
issues.title: Motion entry cannot reach Accelerating operationally

issues.basis: NL9; Approaching source/model identity; finite reachability facts for InMotion and Approaching; event-consumer facts showing all Approaching consumers are unreachable.
issues.expected: While in Approaching, the system must continue to approach the destination.
issues.observed: Approaching is unreachable from the root initial entry. Its closed-model event consumers exist for Arrived_Stop_SendArrived and Obstacle_Detected, but neither consumer is reachable.
issues.reason: The source requires ongoing behavior in Approaching, but the exact state is unreachable from the root initial entry. issues.strongest_rebuttal: Approaching has outgoing transitions in the closed model, so the evidence does not establish a zero-outgoing deadlock; it establishes failure of operational reachability for the required state behavior.
issues.title: Approaching has no reachable operational continuation

report_issue_clusters.observed: The following transitions realise the condition the requirement states as a guard by writing it as the transition label, i.e. as the trigger event: (1) DoorsClosing -> InMotion: label `Closed/SendDeparted`, required guard 'the doors are closed' (PlantUML line 4: `DoorsClosing --> InMotion: Closed/SendDeparted`) (2) Accelerating -> Cruising: label `Reached Cruising/Cruise`, required guard 'cruising speed is reached' (PlantUML line 8: `Accelerating --> Cruising : Reached Cruising/Cruise`) (3) Accelerating -> Approaching: label `Approached/Decelerate`, required guard 'approaches its destination' (PlantUML line 9: `Accelerating --> Approaching : Approached/Decelerate`) (4) Cruising -> Approaching: label `Approached/Decelerate`, required guard 'approaches the destination' (PlantUML line 10: `Cruising --> Approaching : Approached/Decelerate`) In PlantUML a label without brackets is the trigger; the closed model therefore declares one opaque event named after each condition and none of these transitions has a guard. Author source: PlantUML line 2: state `DoorsClosing` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 6: state `InMotion` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 4: `DoorsClosing --> InMotion: Closed/SendDeparted`; PlantUML line 12: state `Accelerating` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 13: state `Cruising` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 8: `Accelerating --> Cruising : Reached Cruising/Cruise`; PlantUML line 14: state `Approaching` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 9: `Accelerating --> Approaching : Approached/Decelerate`; PlantUML line 10: `Cruising --> Approaching : Approached/Decelerate`.
